#host1: # Pakistan Telecom BGP prefix hijack — February 2008.
# PT announced a more-specific /25 within YouTube's /24
# attracting traffic for that range to PT and blackholing it.
# Roles:
#   YouTube     — victim; content provider; originates 208.65.153.0/24; customer of Tier1
#   Tier1       — Tier-1 backbone; provider of YouTube
#   PCCW        — Tier-1/backbone; peer of Tier1; provider of PT and ISP;
#                 the critical propagator — accepts PT's /25 as customer route
#                 and re-advertises it to peer Tier1 and customer ISP
#   PT  — attacker; customer of PCCW; announces 208.65.153.128/25 as self-originated
#   ISP         — observer; customer of PCCW; experiences partial blackhole to YouTube's prefix
# Key mechanism:
#   1. YouTube originates 208.65.153.0/24 → Tier1 → PCCW → {PT
#   2. PT announces 208.65.153.128/25 to PCCW as self-originated (no AS-path)
#   3. PCCW accepts as customer route (highest local-pref) and propagates to Tier1 and ISP
#   4. Longest-prefix match: /25 overrides /24 for 208.65.153.128-255 range
#   5. Traffic to 208.65.153.128-255 → PCCW → PT → blackhole
#   6. No MOAS: /24 and /25 are different prefixes — no direct conflict visible
#   7. Detection requires recognizing that /25 is a sub-prefix of YouTube's /24
#      and that PT has no right to announce a sub-allocation of it
